rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among them” means in the Muslim community.
rows.anchor: أي أرسل في الأمة المسلمة وقيل : في الذرية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes “among them” to mean among Abraham’s descendants.
rows.anchor: أي أرسل في الأمة المسلمة وقيل : في الذرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Referring the pronoun to the people of Mecca is far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وعود الضمير إلى أهل مكة بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger from their own people would be compassionate, honored, and readily believed because they knew his origins, truthfulness, and trustworthiness.
rows.anchor: ووصفه بذلك ليكون أشفق عليهم ويكونوا أعز به واشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only Muhammad descended from both Abraham and Ishmael; the other Israelite prophets descended from Abraham, not from both, so Muhammad fulfilled their joint prayer.
rows.anchor: ولم يبعث من ذرية كليهما سوى محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said he was Abraham’s prayer, Jesus’s glad tidings, and the vision his mother saw at his birth; al-Alusi cites Ahmad and Sharh al-Sunna without grading it.
rows.anchor: عن العرباض عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال : سأخبركم بأول أمري أنا دعوة إبراهيم وبشارة عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Abraham’s prayer” may mean its outcome, its recipient, or the very prayer itself by emphatic expression.
rows.anchor: وأراد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إثر دعوته أو مدعوه أو عين دعوته على المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Ishmael shared the supplication, Muhammad was Ishmael’s prayer too; Abraham is named for nobility and his foundational role in the supplication.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم دعوة إسماعيل أيضا إلا أنه خص إبراهيم لشرافته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the claim that naming only Abraham in the hadith proves Ishmael’s prayer was not answered.
rows.anchor: وهم من قال : إن الإقتصار في الحديث على إبراهيم يدل على أن المجاب

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy read “and raise among them, among their last ones, a messenger,” supporting identification with Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( وأبعث فيهم في آخرهم رسولا ) وهذا يويد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are revealed proofs of divine oneness, prophethood, and related truths, recited by the messenger.
rows.anchor: من العلامات الدالة على التوحيد والنبوة وغيرهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the signs as reports of past and future events through the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل : خبر من مضى ومن يأتي إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recitation clause is either an adjective of “messenger” or a circumstantial clause referring to him.
rows.anchor: والجملة صفة ( رسولا ) وقيل : في موضع الحال منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching the Book means explaining its wording and mode of recitation, and acquainting them with its realities and secrets.
rows.anchor: بأن يفهمهم ألفاظه ويبين لهم كيفية أدائه ويوقفهم على حقائقه وأسراره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer’s apparent aim is a scripture-bearing messenger leading people from ignorance to knowledge; the Qur’an fulfills it, though its being specifically requested is not explicit.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الرسول صاحب كتاب يخرجهم من ظلمة الجهل إلى نور العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed sense of wisdom is putting things in their proper places.
rows.anchor: والحكمة أي وضع الأشياء مواضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed sense is what removes the heart’s ardent attachment to worldly life.
rows.anchor: ما يزيل من القلوب وهج حب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is also explained as religious jurisprudence or the Sunna that clarifies the Book.
rows.anchor: أو الفقه في الدين أو السنة المبينة للكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take wisdom as the Book itself, repeated for emphasis and care.
rows.anchor: وكرر للتأكيد إعتناء بشأنه وقد يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom may mean the Book’s embedded truths and subtleties, with teaching its wording and wisdom its inner contents.
rows.anchor: المراد بها حقائق الكتاب ودقائقه وسائر ما أودع فيه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some define wisdom as knowledge and rulings by which souls are perfected theoretically and practically.
rows.anchor: وفسرها بعضهم بما تكمل به النفوس من المعارف والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi challenges the claim that some soul-perfecting matters lie outside the Qur’an after declarations that it omits nothing and explains everything; he allows a distinction for the scripture requested before the answer.
rows.anchor: ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification means cleansing them of idolatry, doubt, and sins.
rows.anchor: أي يطهرهم من أرجاس الشرك وأنجاس الشك وقاذورات المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching adorns the soul and purification empties it of defilement; precedence of adornment is attributed to its nobility.
rows.anchor: كما أن التعليم إشارة إلى التحلية ولعل تقديم الثاني على الأول لشرافته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking this as collecting alms from them or attesting to their purity and uprightness is far-fetched.
rows.anchor: والقول بأن المراد يأخذ منهم الزكاة التي هي سبب لطهرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mighty, Wise” means overpowering and effecting whatever He wills; God can single someone out for this mission without an external selector.
rows.anchor: أي الغالب المحكم لما يريد فلك أن تخصص واحدا منهم بالرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi finds distant Ibn Abbas’s gloss of “Mighty” as peerless, al-Kalbi’s as avenger, and “Wise” as simply knowing.
rows.anchor: وحمل ( العزيز ) هنا على من لا مثل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is an independent legal ruling, set apart from earlier rulings to mark its independence.
rows.anchor: بيان حكم آخر من الأحكام المذكورة وفصله عما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted “O believers” is explained by the recent admonition, the link to the preceding discussion of the dead, or the ruling’s lack of hardship.
rows.anchor: ولم يصدره ب ( ياأيها الذين آمنوا ) لقرب العهد بالتنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death’s arrival means either its causes and signs, such as dangerous illnesses, or death itself drawing near.
rows.anchor: حضور أسبابه وظهور أماراته من العلل والأمراض المخوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronting emphasizes how firmly the impending event takes hold of the person’s awareness.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لإفادة كمال تمكن الفاعل عند النفس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid explain “good” as property or wealth.
rows.anchor: أي مالا كما قاله إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه ومجاهد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some restrict “good” to substantial wealth, since ordinary usage reserves “wealthy” for someone with a great deal.
rows.anchor: إذ لا يقال في العرف للمال : ( خيرا ) إلا إذا كان كثيرا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali advised a dying client with six or seven hundred dirhams not to bequeath, citing the substantial-wealth condition; al-Bayhaqi and others transmit it from Urwa.
rows.anchor: أن عليا كرم الله تعالى وجهه دخل على مولى له في الموت وله سبعمائة درهم أو ستمائة درهم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A man with three thousand dirhams and four dependents asked Aisha about bequeathing; she called it little and advised leaving it to his family.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها أن رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether property counts as substantial depends on a person’s circumstances and dependents, not a fixed amount.
rows.anchor: أن الكثرة غير مقدرة بمقدار بل تختلف باختلاف حال الرجل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas sets the threshold at sixty dinars: whoever leaves less has not left “good.”
rows.anchor: من لم يترك ستين دينارا لم يترك خيرا

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri holds that bequest is prescribed whether the estate is small or large, taking “good” to mean property without a size limit.
rows.anchor: ومذهب الزهري أن ( الوصية ) مشروعة مما قل أو كثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi suggests the wording implies that bequests should use lawful, wholesome assets, since illicit property must be returned to its owners.
rows.anchor: ينبغي أن يكون الموصى به حلالا طيبا لا خبيثا

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Radi explains the masculine verb form: omitting the feminine marker is preferable when a separated subject is grammatically but not truly feminine.
rows.anchor: إذا كان الظاهر غير حقيقي التأنيث منفصلا فترك العلامة أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Wasiyya” is the verbal noun and the thing enjoined; al-Qamus gives awṣā and waṣṣā as “to entrust or enjoin.”
rows.anchor: أوصاه ووصاه توصية عهد إليه

rows.speaker: الجمهور والرضي
rows.claim: Most construe the preposition with “wasiyya” through an “an” clause plus verb; al-Radi permits a verbal noun without that reinterpretation and is preferred.
rows.anchor: والجار متعلق بها فلا بد من تأويلها بأن مع الفعل عند الجمهور أو بالمصدر بناءا على تحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes “the bequest” the subject of “was written”; the condition’s omitted answer is supplied by “was written for you.”
rows.anchor: ما المكتوب فقيل هو الوصية وجواب الشرط محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes “the bequest for parents” a nominal conditional answer with an implicit fā; Khalil rejects its omission except in poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ خبره ( للوالدين ) والجملة جواب الشرط بإضمار الفاء

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Khalil rejects dropping the fā from a nominal conditional answer outside poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: إضمار الفاء غير صحيح لا يجتريء عليه إلا في ضرورة الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Was written” can govern “when”; the time phrase limits when the obligation arises while evoking its eternal inscription.
rows.anchor: والظرف قيد للإيجاب من حيث الحدوث والوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parse makes “you” the deputy subject and “the bequest” the predicate, answering “What was written?”
rows.anchor: ما المكتوب فقيل هو الوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase may instead be governed by “the bequest,” construed as a verbal noun or “an” clause; adverbs readily accommodate verbal force.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون العامل الوصية وهي وإن كانت اسما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “One of you” is distributive, making the obligation individual rather than communal.
rows.anchor: يفيد العموم على سبيل البدل فمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is contrasted with the same “written upon you” formula for retaliation at 2:178.
rows.anchor: كتب عليكم القصاص في القتلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the claim that the dying person must bequeath while others must preserve the will; preservation arises only after a will exists.
rows.anchor: بل عليه بأن يوصى وعلى الغير بأن يحفظ ولا يبدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is strained to make “you” mean intending and preserving the bequest instead of the bequest itself.
rows.anchor: إرادة الإيصاء وحفظه من الوصية تعسف لا يخفى

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some investigators treat both clauses as conditions with omitted answers: if death comes, let him bequeath if he leaves property; the second condition qualifies the first.
rows.anchor: وأختار بعض المحققين أن ( إذا ) شرطية وجواب كل من الشرطين محذوف

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: These investigators praise the parse for stating the rule generally, then detailing the required bequest parenthetically.
rows.anchor: ومجموع الشرطين معترض بين ( كتب ) وفاعله لبيان كيفية الإيصاء قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi cautions that the parse requires so many deletions that they weaken its advantages.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم ما في ذلك من كثرة الحذف المهونة لما تقدم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر وقتادة وشريح ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Qatada, Shurayh, Mujahid, and others hold that the original bequest ruling was abrogated by inheritance verses.
rows.anchor: كما قاله إبن عباس وابن عمر وقتادة وشريح ومجاهد وغيرهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said God allotted each person an inheritance share, so no bequest may go to an heir; al-Tirmidhi graded the report sound.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن خارجة رضي الله تعالى عنهم أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم خطبهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Umama says he heard the Prophet at the Farewell Pilgrimage say that God gave every rights-holder their due and there is no bequest to an heir.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي سمعت رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم في حجة الوداع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Abd ibn Humayd transmits a similar statement from Hasan.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says communal acceptance makes these reports recurrent enough for abrogation by his imams; some also infer recurrence from broad transmission or unopposed shared practice.
rows.anchor: لتلقي الأمة لها بالقبول انتظمت في سلك المتواتر في صحة النسخ بها عند أئمتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance verse itself effected abrogation, while the hadith explain how; al-Fakhr al-Islam then gives two arguments.
rows.anchor: على أن النسخ في الحقيقة بآية المواريث والأحاديث مبينة لجهة نسخها

rows.speaker: فخر الإسلام
rows.claim: Al-Fakhr argues that the later inheritance verse says “after a bequest” indefinitely; if the earlier specified bequest still governed, inheritance would follow it, so the unrestricted wording abrogates it.
rows.anchor: من بعد وصية يوصى بها أو دين

rows.speaker: فخر الإسلام
rows.claim: His second argument treats abrogation as transfer: God first required fair bequests among kin, then fixed shares Himself because testators may misjudge or intend harm.
rows.anchor: فرض الإيصاء في الأقربين إلى العباد بشرط أن يراعوا الحدود

rows.speaker: فخر الإسلام
rows.claim: The fixed inheritance shares replace delegated bequests with God’s wiser allotment, like a principal freeing a slave after instructing an agent to do so.
rows.anchor: على وجه تيقن به أنه الصواب وأن فيه الحكمة البالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fā in the inheritance passage signals that the earlier bequest scheme caused the transfer to inheritance.
rows.anchor: الفاء تدل على سببية ما قبلها لما بعدها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some argue the inheritance verse confirms bequests by giving them priority, and object that solitary reports are not made recurrent by communal acceptance.
rows.anchor: آية المواريث لا تعارض هذا الحكم بل تحققه من حيث تدل على تقديم الوصية مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects anti-abrogation readings that identify the bequest with God’s inheritance allotment or the decedent’s duty to execute it.
rows.anchor: على ما فيه بمعزل عن التحقيق وكذا ما قيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says bequests to heirs were obligatory without fixed shares, then God’s own bequest of inheritance shares replaced the former delegation.
rows.anchor: من أن الوصية للوارث كانت واجبة بهذه الآية من غير تعيين لأنصبائهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas holds that the duty was abrogated only for inheriting relatives and remained binding for non-inheriting relatives, such as non-Muslim kin.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهب إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali warns that dying without a bequest for non-inheriting relatives ends one’s work in disobedience.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه من لم يوص عند موته لذوي قرابته ممن لا يرث

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most hold that obligation was abrogated for everyone, while bequests to non-inheriting relatives remain recommended.
rows.anchor: وهي مستحبة في حق الذين لا يرثون وإليه ذهب الأكثرون

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan infers that “relatives” alone does not include parents because the verse coordinates parents and relatives.
rows.anchor: وأستدل محمد بن الحسن بالآية على أن مطلق الأقربين لا يتناول الوالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “As a duty” is a cognate accusative emphasizing “was written,” governed either by that verb or an implicit “it is truly due.”
rows.anchor: مصدر مؤكد للحدث الذي دل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Upon the God-fearing” can modify the accusative or the implicit verb; a verbal noun may also govern it directly.
rows.anchor: صفة له أو متعلق بالفعل المحذوف على المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The God-fearing” means believers; the explicit description marks carrying out a bequest as a trait of those who fear God.
rows.anchor: ووضع المظهر موضع المضمر للدلالة على أن المحافظة على الوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The month of Ramadan” may be the subject, with the relative clause as predicate, introducing the obligation by the month’s merit.
rows.anchor: رمضان ) مبتدأ خبره الموصول بعده ويكون ذكر الجملة مقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “whoever witnesses the month” is the predicate, with fā licensed by its conditional sense.
rows.anchor: والفاء لتضمنه معنى الشرط لكونه موصوفا بالموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may predicate an omitted “that is the time when fasting was prescribed,” or identify the prescribed month.
rows.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف تقديره ذلكم الوقت الذي كتب عليكم الصيام فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may be whole-apposition to fasting, estimating “fasting the month of Ramadan”; the intervening words still relate to “was prescribed.”
rows.anchor: بدل كل بتقدير مضاف أي كتب عليكم الصيام صيام شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inclusion-apposition avoids estimating a genitive, but is less fitting because the previous fasting ruling is the main point and does not anticipate an apposition.
rows.anchor: وإن اعتبرته بدل اشتمال استغنيت عن التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with “month” in the accusative construes it as the object of an omitted “fast.”
rows.anchor: وقريء ( شهر ) بالنصب على أنه مفعول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another accusative parse makes it object of “that you fast,” but this separates parts of the verbal noun construction.
rows.anchor: مفعول ( وأن تصوموا ) وفيه لزوم الفصل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is also parsed as object of “you know,” estimating the month’s merit; a literal reading means knowing the month itself, which al-Alusi rejects.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون مفعول ( تعلمون ) بتقدير مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A month is a period beginning with sighting the new moon; “ashhur” is the plural for a few and “shuhur” for many.
rows.anchor: المدة المعينة التي ابتداؤها رؤية الهلال ويجمع في القلة على أشهر وفي الكثرة على شهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Month” derives from a root meaning that something appeared, as months mark worship and transactions and become publicly known.
rows.anchor: وأصله من شهر الشيء أظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi accepts Ramadan as a verbal noun from “to burn”; he faults al-Bahr for denying verbal nouns from intransitive verbs.
rows.anchor: فما في البحر من أن كونه مصدرا يحتاج إلى نقل

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil derives Ramadan from “ramad,” a pre-autumn rain that cleans the earth of dust.
rows.anchor: والخليل يقول : إنه من الرمضمسكن الميموهو مطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the compound month-name conventionally applies to Ramadan and the two Rabi months.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة فقد أطبقوا على أن العلم في ثلاثة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mnemonic says “month” is added only before names beginning with rāʾ, except Rajab, where that usage was not heard.
rows.anchor: وقد نظم ذلك بعضهم فقال : ولا تضف شهرا إلى اسم شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compound analysis derives rules for declension and the article from the second element.
rows.anchor: في الإضافة يعتبر في أسباب منع الصرف وإمتناع اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that account, bare “Ramadan” in “whoever fasts Ramadan” drops one element of the compound to avoid ambiguity.
rows.anchor: فنحو من صام رمضان من حذف جزء العلم لعدم الإلباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acceptability of adding a generic noun to a specific one depends on usage and taste, not an absolute rule.
rows.anchor: ولهذا تحسن تارة كشجر الأراك وتقبح أخرى كإنسان زيد

rows.speaker: أكثر النحويين
rows.claim: Most grammarians allow “month” to be added to every month-name, contrary to the claim that only three such forms are attested.
rows.anchor: شرح التسهيل جواز إضافة ( شهر ) إلى جميع أسماء الشهور

rows.speaker: أدب الكاتب
rows.claim: Adab al-Katib describes the limited forms as a scribal convention from Umar’s calendar, not a rule of language.
rows.anchor: من أنه أصطلاح الكتاب قال : لأنهم لما

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh allows “month” with all month-names: including it is non-generic, while omitting it gives the generic sense.
rows.anchor: وفرق بين ذكره وعدمه بأنه حيث ذكر

rows.speaker: النحاة
rows.claim: Grammarians report both declinable and indeclinable “Ibn Dayah”; a cited verse illustrates the form, with competing compound analyses.
rows.anchor: ولما رأيت النسر عزإبن داية وعشش في وكريه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi concludes that Ramadan alone is a generic proper name for the known month.
rows.anchor: المعول عليه أن ( رمضان ) وحده علم وهو علم جنس

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra, both attributed to the Prophet and stopped at the Companion, forbids saying “Ramadan” because it is a divine name; say “month of Ramadan.”
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا وموقوفا لا تقولوا : رمضان فإن رمضان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid adopts the prohibition on saying “Ramadan” alone.
rows.anchor: إلى ذلك ذهب مجاهدوالصحيح الجواز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi’s correct view permits “Ramadan” alone, citing its use in sound hadith, while acknowledging caution.
rows.anchor: الجوازفقد روى ذلك في الصحيح والإحتياط لا يخفى

rows.speaker: ابن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Amr explains the name by saying sins are burned away in that month.
rows.anchor: لأن الذنوب ترمض فيهقاله إبن عمرو

rows.speaker: أنس وعائشة
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet through Anas and Aisha also explains the name by sins burning in Ramadan.
rows.anchor: وروى ذلك أنس وعائشة مرفوعا إلى النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the month fell during burning heat when ancient month-names were transferred; its old name was Natiq.
rows.anchor: لوقوعه أيام رمض الحر حيث نقلوا أسماء الشهور عن اللغة القديمة

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says revelation of the Qur’an began in Ramadan on the Night of Power.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك ليلة القدرقاله إبن إسحاق وروي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Hasan say the Qur’an descended all at once to the lowest heaven, then gradually to earth over twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وإبن جبير والحسن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view understands the Qur’an’s descent in Ramadan as the revelation about Ramadan, namely the command to fast.
rows.anchor: أنزل في شأنه القرآن وهو قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Wathila says Abraham’s scrolls descended on Ramadan’s first night, the Torah on the sixth, the Gospel on the thirteenth, and the Qur’an on the twenty-fourth; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: من حديث وائلة بن الأسقع عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting is a great sign of servitude and removes human attachments that block divine illumination, so the month of revealed scriptures is suited to fasting.
rows.anchor: بين الصوم ونزول الكتب الإلهية مناسبة عظيمة

words: هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٍ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Guidance” and “clear proofs” are circumstantial clauses describing the Qur’an, governed by “was sent down.”
rows.anchor: هدى للناس وبينات من الهدى والفرقان حالان لازمان من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an guides people through its uniquely inimitable character.
rows.anchor: هداية للناس بإعجازه المختص به كما يشعر بذلك التنكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also contains clear signs shared with other revealed books, guiding to truth and distinguishing it from falsehood through divine knowledge and practical rulings.
rows.anchor: آيات واضحات من جملة الكتب الإلهية الهادية إلى الحق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view repeats “guidance” for glorification and emphasis, like saying “a learned expert.”
rows.anchor: وقيل : مكرر تنويها وتعظيما لأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whoever” may be conditional or relative; the fā is either the conditional answer or extra in the predicate.
rows.anchor: من شرطية أو موصولة والفاء إما جواب الشرط أو زائدة في الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among you” is circumstantial to the implicit subject of “witnessed,” excluding children and the insane.
rows.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال من المستكن في ( شهد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Witnessed” can mean physical presence or knowledge of the month; both senses are proposed.
rows.anchor: من الشهود والتركيب يدل على الحضور إما ذاتا أو علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On physical presence, “the month” is a temporal adverb and the direct object is omitted as irrelevant, not supplied as a town or country.
rows.anchor: على الأول مفعول فيه والمفعول به متروك لعدم تعلق الغرض به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the knowledge reading, it is the object with “crescent of” understood; the definite article refers to the known crescent.
rows.anchor: وعلى الثاني مفعول به بحذف المضاف أي هلال الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit noun replaces a pronoun to honor the month.
rows.anchor: ووضع المظهر موضع المضمر للتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attached pronoun is accusative by extended usage although “to fast” is normally intransitive.
rows.anchor: على الاتساع لأن صام لازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the presence reading, a non-traveler present during Ramadan must fast; on the knowledge reading, whoever knows the crescent with certainty must fast.
rows.anchor: فمن حضر في الشهر ولم يكن مسافرا فليصم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge reading implies that fasting is not obligatory when the new moon is uncertain.
rows.anchor: عدم وجوب الصوم على من شك في الهلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing the whole month would occur only after it ended, motivating the estimate “crescent” on the knowledge reading.
rows.anchor: إنما قدر المضاف لأن شهود الشهر بتمامه إنما يكون بعد انقضائه

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sick-and-traveler concession specifies both groups on the knowledge reading, but only the sick on the presence reading because travelers were already excluded.
rows.anchor: وعلى الأول مخصص بالنظر إلى الأول دون الثاني

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated concession serves that specification or prevents an assumption of abrogation, linking back to the earlier fasting verse.
rows.anchor: لئلا يتوهم نسخه كما نسخ قرينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers physical presence because it needs no estimated word and places the fā as expected, detailing the earlier general command.
rows.anchor: ورجح المعنى الأول من المعنيين بعدم الاحتياج إلى التقدير
